author: Epiphanius of Salamis
occasion: The surviving fragment is a brief doctrinal statement defending the equal glorification and worship of Father, Son, and Holy Spirit, apparently excerpted from a longer work on the Trinity.
argument: Epiphanius states that Father, Son, and Holy Spirit receive one single doxology and one single act of worship. He supports this by interpreting the seraphim's threefold cry of 'Holy, holy, holy' as glorifying the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit together. The fragment presents this as a statement of Trinitarian worship without further elaboration.

outline.move: The fragment states that Father, Son, and Holy Spirit share one doxology and one worship, and that the seraphim's threefold 'Holy' glorifies all three persons.

cast.name: Epiphanius of Salamis
cast.who: The author, identified in the source as Epiphanius of Cyprus.

cast.name: Seraphim
cast.who: The heavenly beings who cry 'Holy, holy, holy' in worship of God.

voices.speaker: Seraphim (quoted)
voices.how_marked: The seraphim's cry is presented as indirect discourse within a subordinate clause ('when the seraphim glorify God...'), not as a direct quotation marked by a verbum dicendi. The quotation marks in modern editions are editorial.

key_terms.sense: The act of giving glory to God; here the single glorification shared by the three divine persons.
The act of worship or adoration offered to God; here one worship offered to the Trinity.
The seraphim's act of glorifying God in their threefold cry.
The cry of the seraphim, repeated three times and interpreted as addressed to the three divine persons.
The first person of the Trinity.
The second person of the Trinity, the Son.
The third person of the Trinity, the Holy Spirit.

scripture: The fragment alludes to the seraphim's cry from Isaiah 6:3. The author uses the Septuagint form 'ἅγιος, ἅγιος, ἅγιος' (Holy, holy, holy). Cite as Isaiah 6:3.
uncertain: The original date of composition is not indicated in the fragment.
The original addressee or audience is not stated in the fragment.
The exact original context within the longer work 'On the Trinity' is not recoverable from this excerpt.
Whether Epiphanius held the title 'bishop of Salamis' at the time of writing is not stated in the source.

_unresolved_facts.claim: The seraphim's cry is presented as indirect discourse within a subordinate clause ('when the seraphim glorify God...'), not as a direct quotation marked by a verbum dicendi. The quotation marks in modern editions are editorial.
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: ὅτε γὰρ δοξολογοῦσι τὰ σεραφὶμ τὸν θεὸν "ἅγιος, ἅγιος, ἅγιος"
_unresolved_facts.fix: The seraphim's cry is presented as direct quotation marked by quotation marks in the source text itself ("ἅγιος, ἅγιος, ἅγιος"), following the temporal conjunction ὅτε with the verb δοξολογοῦσι. The quotation marks appear in the transmitted Greek text, not merely as editorial additions in modern editions.

_unresolved_facts.source_quote: ὅτε γὰρ δοξολογοῦσι τὰ σεραφὶμ τὸν θεὸν "ἅγιος, ἅγιος, ἅγιος"
_unresolved_facts.fix: The seraphim are not given a speaking voice per se; rather, their act of glorifying (δοξολογοῦσι) is described, with the content of their glorification quoted directly. The brief should clarify that the seraphim are the subject of a third-person description by Epiphanius, not a speaking 'voice' in the text.
